instructions: Put 3/4 cup pecans in a dry skillet over medium low. Toast them for 3 to 5 minutes, tossing often, until they smell toasty and turn a shade darker. Tip them onto a board to cool.
Meanwhile, pull the meat off the chicken, leaving the skin and bones behind, and dice enough to fill 3 cups. Keep the rest of the chicken for another meal.
Halve 1 1/2 cups of the grapes. Cut 2 celery stalks in half lengthwise, then slice them thin. Finely chop about a quarter of the red onion.
Coarsely chop the cooled pecans and chop 1 1/2 tbsp of the dill.
Put the chicken, grapes, celery, onion and pecans in a large bowl.
In a small bowl, stir together 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 1/3 cup sour cream, the dill, 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp pepper. Squeeze in 1 1/2 tbsp juice from the lemon.
Pour the dressing over the chicken and stir until everything is coated. Taste it, and add a pinch more salt or a squeeze more of the lemon if it's flat.
Wash and dry 4 lettuce leaves. Lay a leaf on each of 4 slices of bread, pile a quarter of the chicken salad on top and close each sandwich with one of the other 4 slices.

For a packed lunch, keep the chicken salad in a container in the fridge and build the sandwich when you eat. The bread goes soggy if it sits with the filling overnight. The chicken salad keeps for 3 days.
Cut the sandwiches in half and serve.
method_notes: All three read versions bind cooked chicken and celery in a mayonnaise dressing brightened with lemon and fresh herbs. Natasha's Kitchen adds red grapes, red onion and toasted pecans and mixes the mayonnaise half and half with sour cream and dill. RecipeTin Eats shreds the chicken fine, uses walnuts, pickles and onion and garlic powder, and Once Upon a Chef keeps it to scallions, dill and parsley with a little sugar and Dijon. This one follows Natasha's Kitchen, scaled to 4 sandwiches, with rotisserie chicken and lettuce on sandwich bread.
